title: Two-Way Prepositions
subtitle: Toggle between Static Location (Dative) and Directional Movement (Accusative) until the intuition clicks.

cheatSheet.summary: Nine spatial prepositions (in, an, auf, unter, über, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen) can take EITHER Dative OR Accusative depending on one crystal-clear question: Is it a static location or a change of place?
keyTakeaways: Ask 'Wo?' (Where is it resting?) → Static Location → DATIVE (im, am, auf dem, in der).
Ask 'Wohin?' (Where is it moving to?) → Directional Movement → ACCUSATIVE (ins, ans, auf den, in die).
Verb pairs give instant clues: liegen/stehen/sitzen/hängen = Static (Wo? → Dative); legen/stellen/setzen/hängen = Movement (Wohin? → Accusative).

patterns.example: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
patterns.translation: The book is lying on the table.

patterns.example: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
patterns.translation: I put the book onto the table.
We are going into the cinema.

cheatSheet.watchOut: Moving AROUND inside the same place ('Ich laufe im Park') is still 'Wo?' (Dative)! You only use Accusative when crossing a boundary into a new destination ('Ich laufe in den Park').

staticExample.german: Die Tasse steht auf dem Tisch.
staticExample.english: The cup is standing on the table.

motionExample.german: Ich stelle die Tasse auf den Tisch.
motionExample.english: I place the cup onto the table.

exercises.english: I put my phone onto the table.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich lege mein Handy auf den Tisch.
exercises.rulePill: 'legen' expresses movement to a destination (Wohin?) → Accusative → Masculine [M] 'der Tisch' becomes 'auf den Tisch'.

staticExample.english: We are already sitting in the cinema.

motionExample.german: Wir gehen heute Abend ins Kino.
motionExample.english: We are going to the cinema tonight.

exercises.english: My brother is working inside the cinema right now.
exercises.fullGerman: Mein Bruder arbeitet gerade im Kino.
exercises.rulePill: 'arbeiten' happens at a static location (Wo?) → Dative → Neuter [N] 'in + dem' contracts to 'im Kino'.

staticExample.german: Das Poster hängt an der Wand.
staticExample.english: The poster is hanging on the wall.

motionExample.german: Sie hängt das Poster an die Wand.
motionExample.english: She hangs the poster onto the wall.

exercises.english: A beautiful painting is hanging on the wall.
exercises.fullGerman: Ein schönes Gemälde hängt an der Wand.
exercises.rulePill: Static position (Wo hängt es?) → Dative → Feminine [F] 'die Wand' becomes 'an der Wand'.

staticExample.german: Die Katze schläft unter dem Bett.
staticExample.english: The cat is sleeping under the bed.

motionExample.german: Die Katze kriecht unter das Bett.
motionExample.english: The cat crawls under the bed.

exercises.english: The ball rolls quickly under the bed.
exercises.fullGerman: Der Ball rollt schnell unter das Bett.
exercises.rulePill: The ball is moving into a new spot (Wohin rollt er?) → Accusative → Neuter [N] stays 'unter das Bett'.

staticExample.german: Die Lampe steht neben dem Sofa.
staticExample.english: The lamp stands next to the sofa.

motionExample.german: Ich stelle die Lampe neben das Sofa.
motionExample.english: I place the lamp next to the sofa.

exercises.english: Our small table stands next to the sofa.
exercises.fullGerman: Unser kleiner Tisch steht neben dem Sofa.
exercises.rulePill: 'stehen' describes a static resting position (Wo?) → Dative → Neuter [N] 'das Sofa' becomes 'neben dem Sofa'.

exercises.promptHint: Look closely at the verb 'legen' (movement) vs. the article!
exercises.english: Please put the keys onto the table.
exercises.fullGerman: Bitte leg die Schlüssel auf den Tisch.
exercises.rulePill: 'legen' is directional movement (Wohin?) → 'auf' triggers Accusative → Masculine [M] 'auf den Tisch'.

staticExample.german: Das Paket liegt vor der Tür.
staticExample.english: The package is lying in front of the door.

motionExample.german: Der Bote stellt das Paket vor die Tür.
motionExample.english: The courier places the package in front of the door.

exercises.prompt: Stell die nassen Schuhe bitte ___ Tür!
exercises.english: Please put the wet shoes in front of the door!
exercises.fullGerman: Stell die nassen Schuhe bitte vor die Tür!
exercises.rulePill: 'stellen' moves an object to a target spot (Wohin?) → Accusative → Feminine [F] stays 'vor die Tür'.

exercises.prompt: Am Sonntag jogge ich gern ___ Park.
exercises.english: On Sunday I like jogging inside the park.
exercises.fullGerman: Am Sonntag jogge ich gern im Park.

nouns.caseTrigger: Activity happening INSIDE one location (Wo?) → Dative

exercises.rulePill: Jogging inside the park doesn't cross into a new destination—it answers 'Wo?' → Dative 'in + dem = im Park'.

exercises.english: She puts the vase onto the shelf.
exercises.fullGerman: Sie stellt die Vase auf das Regal.
